questions.stem:
A manufacturer performed an analysis of its product's price point in an effort to meet its customers' demand without experiencing excess inventory.

Price Point | Supply | Demand
$4 | 20 | 10
$3 | 15 | 15
$2 | 10 | 20
$1 | 5 | 25

The manufacturer uses just-in-time inventory processes, and demand for the product is elastic. Which of the following prices should management use in order to address the efforts above while maximizing profits?
questions.explanation: Excess inventory appears when supply exceeds demand, and lost sales appear when demand exceeds supply, so the price that avoids both is the one where supply equals demand: $3, at 15 units each. Units actually sold at each price are the lesser of supply and demand, so revenue is $40 at $4 (10 units sold, 10 left over), $45 at $3, $20 at $2 (10 units, shortage of 10) and $5 at $1 (5 units, shortage of 20). The $3 price gives the highest revenue and leaves no unsold inventory, which also suits a just-in-time process.
questions.explanationJa: 供給と需要が一致する価格が、売れ残りも品切れも出さない価格で、$3（供給・需要とも15単位）。各価格での販売量は供給と需要の小さいほうなので、売上は$4が$40（10単位売れ10単位が余る）、$3が$45、$2が$20（供給10単位で品切れ）、$1が$5。$3が売上最大で在庫も余らず、JIT運営にも合う。
references: AICPA BAR Blueprint Area I-B-5 (supply and demand and elasticity)

questions.stem:
A company increased the price of its products and noted subsequent decreases in demand as below:

Product | Price Increase | Demand Decrease
Product A | 20% | 40%
Product B | 30% | 20%

The data above best support which of the following conclusions regarding the price elasticity of demand for the two products?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Product A is treated by consumers as a necessity.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Product B is treated by consumers as a luxury item.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Substitutes are more readily available for Product A than for Product B.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Substitutes are more readily available for Product B than for Product A.

questions.explanation: Price elasticity of demand is the percentage change in quantity demanded divided by the percentage change in price. Product A is 40% / 20% = 2.0, which is elastic, and Product B is 20% / 30% = about 0.67, which is inelastic. Demand is elastic when buyers can switch to substitutes easily, so substitutes are more readily available for Product A. Necessities have inelastic demand, which is the pattern of Product B rather than Product A, and a luxury item would show elastic demand, which is the pattern of Product A rather than Product B.
questions.explanationJa: 価格弾力性＝需要の変化率÷価格の変化率。製品Aは40%÷20%＝2.0で弾力的、製品Bは20%÷30%≒0.67で非弾力的。代替品を容易に入手できるほど需要は弾力的になるので、代替品が手に入りやすいのは製品A。必需品は非弾力的（製品Bの型）で、贅沢品は弾力的（製品Aの型）なので、必需品がA・贅沢品がBという記述はどちらも逆。
references: AICPA BAR Blueprint Area I-B-5 (supply and demand and elasticity)

questions.stem:
Gray Co. and Seas Co. have the following items on their balance sheet at the end of the current year:

Company | Current assets | Current liabilities
Gray Co. | $2,500,000 | $1,000,000
Seas Co. | 5,000,000 | 3,000,000

Which of the following statements best describes the liquidity position of the two companies in relation to each other?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Seas is more liquid because it carries a larger amount of current assets than Gray.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Seas is more liquid because it has working capital greater than Gray.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gray is more liquid because it carries a smaller amount of current liabilities than Seas.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gray is more liquid because it has a larger current ratio than Seas.

questions.explanation: Comparing the liquidity of companies of different size calls for a ratio rather than an absolute amount. The current ratio is $2,500,000 / $1,000,000 = 2.50 for Gray and $5,000,000 / $3,000,000 = about 1.67 for Seas, so Gray has more current assets per dollar of current liabilities. Seas has the larger working capital ($2,000,000 against $1,500,000) and the larger current assets, but those are absolute amounts that grow with company size and say nothing about coverage of short-term obligations.
questions.explanationJa: 規模の異なる会社の流動性は金額ではなく比率で比べる。流動比率はGrayが$2,500,000÷$1,000,000＝2.50、Seasが$5,000,000÷$3,000,000≒1.67で、流動負債1ドルあたりの流動資産はGrayが多い。Seasは運転資本（$2,000,000対$1,500,000）も流動資産も大きいが、これらは規模に比例する絶対額で、短期債務をどれだけカバーできるかは示さない。
references: AICPA BAR Blueprint Area I-A-1 (liquidity ratios)

questions.stem:
Based on the following data, what is the cost of goods sold for the company?

Sales | $1,000,000
Net purchases of raw materials | 600,000
Cost of goods manufactured | 800,000
Marketing and administrative expenses | 250,000
Indirect manufacturing costs | 500,000

Inventory | Beginning | Ending
Work in process | $500,000 | $400,000
Finished goods | 100,000 | 500,000
questions.explanation: Cost of goods sold equals beginning finished goods plus cost of goods manufactured minus ending finished goods: $100,000 + $800,000 - $500,000 = $400,000. The cost of goods manufactured is already given, so the raw material purchases, indirect manufacturing costs and work-in-process balances are not needed, and marketing and administrative expenses are period costs outside cost of goods sold. The $900,000 answer leaves out the ending finished goods, and the $600,000 answer is just the raw material purchases.
questions.explanationJa: 売上原価＝期首製品＋当期製品製造原価－期末製品＝$100,000＋$800,000－$500,000＝$400,000。製品製造原価が与えられているので、材料購入・製造間接費・仕掛品残高は不要で、販売費及び一般管理費は期間費用で売上原価に入らない。$900,000は期末製品を引き忘れた値、$600,000は材料購入額そのもの。
references: AICPA BAR Blueprint Area I-A-3 (managerial and cost accounting)

questions.stem:
A company provides the following information about discount factors and yearly cash flows:

Number | Discount factor | Annual cash flow
1 | .9 | $200
2 | .8 | 400
3 | .7 | 500
4 | .6 | 500

If the discounted payback method is used, an outlay of $1,000 cash would most likely result in payback in which of the following months?
questions.explanation: Discounted payback uses present values of the cash flows: $200 x .9 = $180, $400 x .8 = $320, $500 x .7 = $350 and $500 x .6 = $300. Cumulative present value is $180, $500 and $850 after the first three years, which is still $150 short of the $1,000 outlay. The remaining $150 is half of the fourth year's $300, so payback comes 0.5 year into the fourth year, at 3.5 years or month 42, assuming cash flows arrive evenly through the year. Month 33 is roughly what the undiscounted cash flows give, and month 36 ends the third year while the investment is still unrecovered.
questions.explanationJa: 割引回収期間は各年のCFの現在価値で判定する。$200×.9＝$180、$400×.8＝$320、$500×.7＝$350、$500×.6＝$300。3年目までの累計は$180→$500→$850で、$1,000にあと$150足りない。残り$150は4年目の$300の半分なので、年内に均等にCFが入るとして3.5年＝42か月目に回収される。33か月目は割引しない場合のおおよその値で、36か月目は3年目の終わりでまだ未回収。
references: AICPA BAR Blueprint Area I-B-3 (payback period)

questions.stem:
MultiCo has the following sales mix:

Product | Sales price | Variable costs | Fixed costs | Percent units sold
Shoes | $100 | $25 | $40 | 30%
Swimsuits | 50 | 10 | 20 | 50%
Hats | 40 | 5 | 5 | 20%

What amount is MultiCo's weighted average contribution margin per unit?
questions.explanation: Contribution margin per unit is sales price minus variable cost: $75 for shoes, $40 for swimsuits and $35 for hats. Weighting each by its share of units sold gives ($75 x 30%) + ($40 x 50%) + ($35 x 20%) = $22.50 + $20.00 + $7.00 = $49.50. Fixed costs are not part of contribution margin, and the $63.33 answer is the unweighted average of the three selling prices.
questions.explanationJa: 単位あたり貢献利益＝販売価格－変動費で、靴$75、水着$40、帽子$35。販売数量構成比で加重すると、($75×30%)＋($40×50%)＋($35×20%)＝$22.50＋$20.00＋$7.00＝$49.50。固定費は貢献利益に含めない。$63.33は3製品の販売価格の単純平均。
references: AICPA BAR Blueprint Area I-B-1 (breakeven analysis)

questions.stem:
Estimated sales for the Johnson Co. in the second quarter are shown below by month:

Month | April | May | June
Sales | $70,000 | $40,000 | $50,000

Johnson has a policy of maintaining 40% of the following month's estimated cost of sales on hand in merchandise inventory at the end of each month. The cost of goods sold is 60% of sales. What is the cost of the merchandise inventory that Johnson needs to purchase in May?
questions.explanation: Cost of goods sold is $24,000 in May ($40,000 x 60%) and $30,000 in June ($50,000 x 60%). Ending May inventory is 40% of June cost of sales, or $12,000, and beginning May inventory (the April ending balance) is 40% of May cost of sales, or $9,600. Purchases = cost of goods sold + ending inventory - beginning inventory = $24,000 + $12,000 - $9,600 = $26,400. The $24,000 answer ignores the inventory change entirely.
references: AICPA BAR Blueprint Area I-B-1 (prepare a budget using supportable assumptions)

questions.stem:
A company has determined that its sales to residential home builders tend to vary with changes in the prime interest rate. Sales this year will be $5 million. The following information is available:

Prime interest rate | Probability | Sales growth
Increases 2% | 15% | (20%)
Increases 1% | 40% | 3%
Unchanged | 35% | 5%
Decreases 1% | 10% | 8%

What amount is the expected value of the company's sales for the coming year's budget?
questions.explanation: The expected sales growth is the probability-weighted average: (15% x -20%) + (40% x 3%) + (35% x 5%) + (10% x 8%) = -3.00% + 1.20% + 1.75% + 0.80% = 0.75%. Expected sales are $5,000,000 x 1.0075 = $5,037,500. Using only the most likely scenario (3% growth, or $5,150,000) ignores the possibility of a sharp decline when rates rise by 2%.
references: AICPA BAR Blueprint Area I-B-1 (forecasting and projection; sensitivity and what-if scenarios)

questions.stem: When risk is evaluated, which of the following risk responses is generally considered a sharing response?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rebalancing the asset portfolio to reduce exposure to certain types of losses.

questions.explanation: Under the COSO enterprise risk management framework, a sharing response reduces the likelihood or impact of a risk by transferring or sharing a portion of it with another party, for example through insurance, hedging, outsourcing, joint ventures or syndication agreements. Diversifying product offerings, reallocating capital among operating units and rebalancing the asset portfolio all lower exposure within the entity's own operations, so they are reduction responses rather than sharing responses.
questions.explanationJa: COSOのERMでは、リスクの一部を他者に移転・分担して発生可能性や影響を減らす対応がシェア（共有）で、保険・ヘッジ・外部委託・ジョイントベンチャー・シンジケート契約などが該当する。製品の多様化、事業部間の資本再配分、資産ポートフォリオの組み替えは、自社内でエクスポージャーを下げる対応なので、共有ではなく低減にあたる。
references: COSO Enterprise Risk Management — Integrating with Strategy and Performance
AICPA BAR Blueprint Area I-B-4 (risk management)

questions.stem: Which of the following is a valid method of calculating the internal rate of return?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Calculate the present value of each cash flow for each year and subtract it from the cost of the investment.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Plot three or four combinations of net present value (NPV) and discount rate on a graph, connect the points with a smooth line, and locate the discount rate at which NPV=0.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Calculate the project net income for each year, and then compute a simple average. Average the project's beginning and ending book value. Divide the average net income by the average book value.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Compute the total of the present values of each year's cash flow. Divide the total of the present values by the initial investment.

questions.explanation: The internal rate of return is the discount rate at which the net present value of the project equals zero, so plotting NPV against several trial discount rates and finding where the curve crosses zero is a valid way to estimate it. Subtracting present values from the investment cost produces a net present value at one given rate, not a rate of return. Dividing average net income by average book value is the accounting rate of return, and dividing total present value of cash inflows by the initial investment is the profitability index.
questions.explanationJa: 内部収益率（IRR）は、NPVがゼロになる割引率。複数の割引率でNPVをプロットし、曲線がゼロと交差する点を読み取る方法は有効。現在価値を投資額から引くのは特定の割引率でのNPVを求める計算で、収益率ではない。平均純利益÷平均帳簿価額は会計上の投資利益率、現在価値合計÷初期投資は収益性指数。
references: AICPA BAR Blueprint Area I-B-3 (internal rate of return)

questions.stem:
A company is evaluating four projects as possible investments. All of the projects are for the same activity. The company will select only one project. The company's discount rate for such projects is 10%, and the tax rate is 40%. The company's reinvestment rate is 10%. Additional information about the projects is as follows:

Project | Internal rate of return | Net present value
A | 11% | $210,000
B | 12% | 195,000
C | 13% | 175,000
D | 14% | 200,000

Which project would be most advantageous to the company?
questions.explanation: When projects are mutually exclusive, the one with the highest net present value adds the most to the company's wealth, because NPV measures the dollar value created at the company's required rate of return. Project A has the highest NPV at $210,000 even though its internal rate of return is the lowest of the four. Ranking by IRR can mislead because IRR ignores the scale of the investment, and the reinvestment rate equal to the 10% discount rate is the assumption NPV already makes.
questions.explanationJa: 互いに排他的な案件では、NPVが最大のものが企業価値を最も増やす（NPVは要求収益率での価値創出額を示す）。案件AはIRRが4案件で最低でも、NPVは$210,000で最大。IRRは投資規模を無視するため順位付けを誤らせうる。再投資率が割引率と同じ10%という前提は、NPVがもともと置いている前提と一致する。
references: AICPA BAR Blueprint Area I-B-3 (compare investment alternatives using net present value and internal rate of return)

questions.stem: XBRL has which of the following features?

choices.label: C
choices.text: XBRL does not require the use of tags.

questions.explanation: XBRL (eXtensible Business Reporting Language) attaches a standardized tag to each piece of financial data so that software can identify what the data represents, which allows reports to be compared and analyzed automatically. It is an XML-based markup for business reporting data and requires tags, so it is neither interchangeable with HTML, a language for displaying web pages, nor with SQL, a language for querying databases.
questions.explanationJa: XBRL（拡張可能な事業報告言語）は、財務データの一つ一つに標準化されたタグを付け、ソフトウェアがそのデータの意味を識別できるようにする仕組みで、報告書の自動比較・分析を可能にする。XMLを基にした事業報告用のマークアップでタグが必須。Webページ表示用のHTMLや、データベース照会用のSQLとは別物で、置き換えはできない。
references: Regulation S-T Rule 405
AICPA BAR Blueprint Area II-J (XBRL business reporting)

questions.stem:
Paper Co. budgeted the following amounts for the period:

Budgeted | Quantity | Amount
Sales | 1,000 tons | $4,500,000
Wood purchases | 2,000 tons | 1,600,000

Actual amounts were:

Actual | Quantity | Amount
Sales | 1,200 tons | $4,800,000
Wood purchases | 2,200 tons | 1,980,000

If there were no changes in inventory, what amount would be the usage variance?
questions.explanation: The budget allows 2.0 tons of wood per ton sold (2,000 / 1,000), so actual sales of 1,200 tons allow 2,400 tons of wood. With no inventory change, actual usage equals the 2,200 tons purchased, which is 200 tons less than allowed. The usage variance values that quantity difference at the budgeted price of $800 per ton ($1,600,000 / 2,000 tons), giving 200 x $800 = $160,000 favorable. The $180,000 answer values the 200 tons at the actual price of $900 per ton, which belongs in the price variance rather than the usage variance.
questions.explanationJa: 予算では販売1トンあたり木材2.0トン（2,000÷1,000）なので、実際販売1,200トンの許容量は2,400トン。在庫増減なしなので実際使用量は購入量の2,200トンで、許容量より200トン少ない。使用量差異は数量差を予算単価$800/トン（$1,600,000÷2,000トン）で評価し、200×$800＝$160,000（有利）。$180,000は実際単価$900で評価した誤りで、これは価格差異の領域。
references: AICPA BAR Blueprint Area I-A-3 (variance analysis)

questions.stem:
Clear Plus, Inc. manufactures and sells boxes of pocket protectors. The static budget and the actual results for May are as follows:

 | Actual results | Static budget
Units sold | 12,000 | 10,000
Revenues | $132,000 | $100,000
Variable costs | $70,800 | $60,000
Contribution margin | $61,200 | $40,000
Fixed costs | $32,000 | $30,000
Operating income | $29,200 | $10,000

What amount of operating income will Clear Plus have for May under a flexible budget?
questions.explanation: A flexible budget restates the budget for the actual volume of 12,000 units using budgeted prices and costs. The budgeted contribution margin is $4 per unit ($10 price less $6 variable cost), so it is $4 x 12,000 = $48,000. Budgeted fixed costs stay at $30,000 regardless of volume, giving operating income of $48,000 - $30,000 = $18,000. The $29,200 answer is the actual operating income, and the actual fixed costs of $32,000 do not belong in a budget.
questions.explanationJa: 変動予算は、予算単価・予算原価を実際の販売量12,000単位に当てはめて作り直したもの。予算の単位あたり貢献利益は$4（価格$10－変動費$6）なので、$4×12,000＝$48,000。固定費は操業度にかかわらず予算額の$30,000で、営業利益は$48,000－$30,000＝$18,000。$29,200は実際の営業利益。
references: AICPA BAR Blueprint Area I-A-3 (variance analysis)

questions.stem:
A company normally sells a product for $12 per unit. The plant capacity is 100,000 units per month, and current production is 75,000 units per month. Current costs are as follows:

Cost | Per unit | Total at 75,000 units
Direct materials | $4 | $300,000
Direct labor | 3 | 225,000
Fixed plant facility cost | 2 | 150,000
Shipping costs | 1 | 75,000

The company received a one-time special order for 10,000 units, which would be shipped in bulk to the buyer at a cost of $5,000 (10,000 times $0.50). What amount is the minimum selling price per unit that the company should accept for the special order?
questions.explanation: The plant has spare capacity (75,000 of 100,000 units) and the order is one-time, so only the incremental costs matter. Those are direct materials of $4, direct labor of $3 and bulk shipping of $0.50, for a minimum price of $7.50 per unit. Fixed plant facility cost is unchanged by the order, and the regular $1 per unit shipping cost is replaced by the $0.50 bulk shipping. Adding the fixed cost gives the $9.50 answer, and using the regular shipping cost instead gives $8.00.
questions.explanationJa: 工場に余裕（75,000/100,000単位）があり、単発の注文なので、増分原価だけを考える。直接材料$4、直接労務費$3、一括輸送費$0.50で最低価格は$7.50/単位。固定製造費は注文で変わらず、通常の運送費$1は一括輸送の$0.50に置き換わる。固定費を足すと$9.50、通常の運送費を使うと$8.00になる誤り。
references: AICPA BAR Blueprint Area I-B-3 (make, lease or buy decisions using financial metrics)
AICPA BAR Blueprint Area I-B-5 (opportunity cost)

questions.stem: What is the consequence of tariffs on imports of a product?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lower profits on rival domestic products

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lower cost for the consumer on rival domestic products

choices.label: D
choices.text: Higher cost for the consumer of the imported product

questions.explanation: A tariff is a tax on imported goods, so it raises the price consumers pay for the imported product. With the imported product more expensive, domestic rivals face less price competition and can sell more or raise their own prices, so their profits tend to rise rather than fall and their prices do not drop. Because the price of the product rises, the quantity consumers buy falls rather than rises.
questions.explanationJa: 関税は輸入品への課税なので、消費者が払う輸入品の価格が上がる。輸入品が割高になると国内の競合品は価格競争が和らぎ、販売増や値上げが可能になるので、利益は増えやすく、価格が下がることはない。製品の価格が上がるため、消費量は増えず減る。
references: AICPA BAR Blueprint Area I-B-5 (economic and market influences on business)
questions.source: Proactive 添削課題 BEC1 Q.4 (Macroeconomics:7266)

questions.stem: What will be the likely result of a decline in the value of the U.S. dollar relative to the currencies of the trading partners of the U.S.?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The U.S. trade deficit will increase.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Foreign currencies will depreciate compared to the U.S. dollar.

questions.explanation: A weaker dollar buys fewer units of foreign currency, so U.S. goods become cheaper for foreign buyers and exports rise. Imported goods become more expensive in dollar terms, so imports fall and the trade deficit narrows rather than widens. A fall in the dollar relative to other currencies is the same thing as foreign currencies appreciating against the dollar, not depreciating.
questions.explanationJa: ドル安になると、外国通貨建てで見た米国製品が割安になり、輸出が増える。輸入品はドル建てで割高になるので、輸入は減り、貿易赤字は拡大ではなく縮小する。ドルが他通貨に対して下がることは、他通貨がドルに対して上がる（増価する）ことと同じで、減価ではない。
references: AICPA BAR Blueprint Area I-B-5 (economic and market influences on business)
questions.source: Proactive 添削課題 BEC1 Q.7 (Macroeconomics:7253)

questions.stem: What is the effective interest rate on a loan if a firm borrows $400,000 at 8% and is required to maintain $50,000 as a minimum compensating balance at the bank, based on a 360-day year?
questions.explanation: Annual interest is $400,000 x 8% = $32,000. The $50,000 compensating balance cannot be spent, so the usable loan proceeds are $400,000 - $50,000 = $350,000. The effective rate is $32,000 / $350,000 = about 9.1%. The 8.0% answer is the stated rate and ignores the compensating balance, and the loan term is one year so the 360-day basis does not change the result.
questions.explanationJa: 年間利息は$400,000×8%＝$32,000。補償預金$50,000は使えないので、実際に使える資金は$400,000－$50,000＝$350,000。実効金利＝$32,000÷$350,000≒9.1%。8.0%は表面利率で補償預金を無視した値。期間は1年なので、360日基準は結果を変えない。
references: AICPA BAR Blueprint Area I-B-2 (financing strategies and cost of capital)
questions.source: Proactive 添削課題 BEC2 Q.6 (Financial Management Q26:7374)

questions.stem: Which of the following is a method of slowing down cash outflows?
questions.explanation: A zero-balance account holds no funds of its own. The company moves money from a master account only when checks are presented for payment, so cash stays in the master account (and keeps earning interest) until the last moment, which slows the effective outflow. Electronic funds transfers and wire transfers move money out immediately, so they speed up outflows. A lockbox is a collection tool that speeds up cash inflows, not outflows.
questions.explanationJa: ゼロ残高口座は自前の資金を持たず、小切手が呈示されたときだけ親口座から資金を移す。そのため資金は最後の瞬間まで親口座に残り（利息も稼ぐ）、実質的な支払が遅くなる。電子資金移動や電信送金は資金が即時に出ていくので支払を早める。ロックボックスは回収を早める手段で、支払ではなく入金側。
references: AICPA BAR Blueprint Area I-B-4 (strategies for managing working capital)
questions.source: Proactive 添削課題 BEC2 Q.9 (Financial Management Q7:7295)

questions.stem: Break-even analysis assumes that over the relevant range total
questions.explanation: Break-even analysis rests on linear relationships within the relevant range: total revenue rises in proportion to units sold because the selling price per unit is constant, and total variable cost rises in proportion to volume. Total fixed costs stay constant. Total costs are therefore not unchanged because the variable part moves with volume, fixed costs are flat rather than nonlinear, and variable costs are linear rather than nonlinear.
questions.explanationJa: 損益分岐点分析は、関連範囲内で線形の関係を前提にする。販売単価が一定なので総収益は販売量に比例し、総変動費も操業度に比例する。総固定費は一定。したがって、総原価は変動費部分が動くので「変わらない」わけではなく、固定費は非線形ではなく一定、変動費は非線形ではなく線形。
